engines.name: ferroni
engines.does: Runs Oniguruma's regular expressions in Rust, lookbehind, backreferences, named groups and Unicode classes included, with the multi-pattern scanner that editors and highlighters drive built in.
engines.audience: For anyone who needs Oniguruma's syntax in Rust, from editors and highlighters to any search that leans on lookbehind or backreferences.
engines.proof: Oniguruma is the regex engine behind PHP's mbstring, jq and every TextMate grammar, and its C project ended in April 2025. Ferroni continues the engine in memory-safe Rust, with the vscode-oniguruma scanner built in.

engines.name: ferriki
engines.does: Highlights code with the grammars and themes your editor uses.
engines.audience: For docs sites, blogs, and build tools that render code.
engines.proof: Shiki brought editor-grade highlighting to the web. Ferriki keeps its familiar contract while moving the engine from JavaScript and WASM to native Rust.

engines.name: ferromark
engines.job: Markdown to HTML, sanitized by default
engines.does: Turns Markdown into HTML, sanitized by default, and is among the fastest engines for the job.
engines.audience: For static sites, docs pipelines, and any app that renders what people write.
engines.proof: CommonMark settled what Markdown means. Ferromark carries that contract, plus GFM and sanitized output, into a Rust renderer built for speed.

engines.name: ferrolex
engines.job: Spell checking for text and code
engines.does: Checks spelling in prose and in code, and gives the same suggestions every time.
engines.audience: For editors, linters, and CI checks.
engines.proof: Hunspell set the dictionary standard. Ferrolex reads those dictionaries while adding compiled dictionaries, deterministic suggestions, and code-aware checking.

engines.name: ferrocat
engines.does: Reads, merges, and compiles translation catalogs.
engines.audience: For teams whose translations live in the repository.
engines.proof: gettext taught software to speak in catalogs. Ferrocat carries that model into Git and AI workflows, where merges stay conflict-free and human corrections stay authoritative.
engines.evidence: Upstream-derived conformance cases · ahead of GNU msgmerge and common PO libraries

engines.name: ferralk
engines.what: A glob matcher and file walker
engines.job: Glob matching and parallel filesystem walking
engines.does: Matches glob patterns and walks file trees in parallel, ahead of globset and fast-glob.
engines.audience: For build tools, linters, and anything that starts with a file list.
engines.proof: Every build tool pays for finding files before it does any work. Ferralk keeps zlob's byte-first approach in pure Rust, without Zig or a C ABI, and holds its matcher and walker to a frozen zlob reference.
engines.evidence: Frozen zlob reference · ahead of globset and fast-glob

engines.name: ferrugo
engines.does: Renders previews of PDF files you have no reason to trust.
engines.audience: For upload pipelines and document viewers.
engines.proof: PDF previews have traditionally meant embedding a browser-sized engine. Ferrugo takes a narrower path: render untrusted files under explicit resource limits, without PDFium.
engines.evidence: Bounded memory and time · no PDFium
